record.original_question: Can SL(n, C) be holomorphically immersed in C^n −1 . [Cannot be done algebraically, true if n=2]

evidence.quote: Problem 9.5.2 Can SL(n, C) be holomorphically immersed in Cn −1 . [Cannot be done algebraically, true if n=2] -R. Narasimhan, Dept. of Math., Univ. of Chicago, Chicago, IL 60637

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 2$ and consider the special linear group $\mathrm{SL}(n,\mathbb{C}) = \{A \in M_n(\mathbb{C}) : \det A = 1\}$, regarded as a complex Stein manifold of complex dimension $n^2 - 1$. Determine whether there exists a holomorphic immersion $f : \mathrm{SL}(n,\mathbb{C}) \to \mathbb{C}^{n^2 - 1}$, i.e., a holomorphic map whose differential $df_p$ has rank $n^2 - 1$ at every point $p \in \mathrm{SL}(n,\mathbb{C})$.

It is known that no such immersion exists in the algebraic category, and that the case $n = 2$ admits an affirmative answer (a holomorphic immersion $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{C}) \to \mathbb{C}^3$ exists). The question is whether, for every $n \geq 3$, $\mathrm{SL}(n,\mathbb{C})$ can be holomorphically immersed into $\mathbb{C}^{n^2 - 1}$.
artifact.status_search_result: A search did not turn up a definitive resolution of whether $\mathrm{SL}(n,\mathbb{C})$ admits a holomorphic immersion into $\mathbb{C}^{n^2-1}$ for general $n \geq 3$. Related progress on optimal-dimension holomorphic immersions of Stein manifolds (e.g., work by Forstnerič, Eliashberg–Gromov, and others on immersions into $\mathbb{C}^N$ with $N$ near $\dim_{\mathbb{C}}$) exists, but no source clearly identifying a solution to this specific question for $\mathrm{SL}(n,\mathbb{C})$ was located.

status_evidence.title: Holomorphic embeddings and immersions of Stein manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of holomorphic embeddings and immersions of Stein manifolds into Euclidean spaces of nearly minimal dimension.
status_evidence.claim: General results on holomorphic immersions of Stein manifolds in low-dimensional Euclidean spaces exist but no explicit resolution for SL(n,C) is stated.

status_evidence.title: Proper holomorphic immersions into Stein manifolds with the density property
status_evidence.snippet: Every Stein manifold S admits a proper holomorphic immersion into any Stein manifold of dimension 2·dim(S) enjoying the density property.
status_evidence.claim: Existing immersion theorems target dimension 2·dim(S), not the critical dimension dim(S)=n^2-1 asked here.
